name: belt_to_nowhere
description: THE WARNING, IN THE FRAME A PLAYER ACTUALLY SEES. A critic read the reference run's four belt lines — three of them reporting `blocked` for 80% of the run, two of them ending in `sink_id: -1` — as belts going nowhere. They are not: lines 1-3 are one compressed chain out of the coal yard whose last tile is bare ground behind the last arm, and line 4 ends under the last of four arms on the Hearth's south face. All four are working belts with more supply than demand, which is what a FULL BELT MEANS. But nothing in the build could say so, which is why the question got asked and answered wrong. This scenario builds the two mistakes for real, so the answer is a photograph rather than an argument: a seven-tile belt loaded out of a crate with nothing at its end and no arm anywhere on it, and a second arm lifting coal out of a second crate and reaching into open snow. Read the run: logistics.lines_to_nowhere is 1 and logistics.arms_no_target is 1 for the whole of it, the log names both by cell, and the ATTENTION panel in shots/named.png carries 'This belt ends in open ground and nothing takes anything off it.' The 'still_building' shot at tick 200 is the other half of the claim and matters just as much: the state is already 1, the panel is SILENT, because every belt is a belt to nowhere for the second between the first tile and the second and an assistant that shouts at a player mid-drag is worse than no assistant. Coordinates are the ones tests/logistics/cold_snap.json already proved buildable on seed 7. It lives here rather than in tests/scenarios/ because that folder is generated by tools/gen_scenarios.py and belongs to [P00].
